An '''epicheireme''' ({{IPAc-en|ɛ|p|i|ˈ|k|aɪ|r|i|m}} {{respell|e|pee|KEYE|reem}}){{efn|plural "epicheirema" {{IPAc-en|ɛ|p|i|k|aɪ|'|r|i|m|ə}} {{respell|e|pee|keye|REEM|ə}}}} is a compound [[syllogism]] in which at least one of the premises is stated along with a justification for itself.<ref name="maritain">{{cite book |title=Formal Logic | page=253 | author=J. Maritain | publisher=Sheed & Ward | asin=B0007F0HL0}}</ref><ref name="cothran">{{cite book|author=Martin Cothran|title=Traditional Logic II|pages=75|year=2017|publisher=[[Memoria Press]]}}</ref> Epicheirema are abridged [[polysyllogism]]s.<ref>{{cite book |title=The Trivium - The Liberal Arts of Logic, Grammar, and Rhetoric | page=145|author=Sister Miriam Joseph, C.S.C., Ph.D. | publisher=PAUL DRY BOOKS |isbn=978-0967967509}}</ref> Like the [[enthymeme]], epicheirema are often used in everyday speech.{{cn|date=September 2024}}

== Basic form ==
An epicheireme is a compound [[syllogism]] in which at least one of the premises is stated along with a justification for itself. The justificatory portion is referred to as a ''causal proposition'', and is usually introduced by the words "for", "since", or "because". An example of an epicheireme is as follows, with the causal proposition marked in bold italics:<ref name="maritain"/><ref name="cothran"/>
:All waiters are beneficent '''''because they cater to the needs of their customers.'''''
:Darryl is a waiter.
:Therefore, Darryl is beneficent.

== Three kinds of epicheirema ==
Epicheirema are categorized in three varieties, depending on which premise (or premises) contain a causal proposition. In a first order epicheireme, the causal proposition is in the major premise.{{cn|date=September 2024}}

'''First Order Epicheireme'''
:All M are P, '''''since r'''''
:S is M
:Therefore, S is P
(where '''r''' is the justification for the proposition that precedes it)

In a second order epicheireme, the causal proposition is in the minor premise.{{cn|date=September 2024}}

'''Second Order Epicheireme'''
:All M are P
:S is M, '''''since r'''''
:Therefore, S is P

In a third order epicheireme, there are causal propositions in both premises.{{cn|date=September 2024}}

'''Third Order Epicheireme'''
:All M are P, '''''since r<sub>1</sub>'''''
:S is M, '''''since r<sub>2</sub>'''''
:Therefore, S is P

A concrete example of a third order epicheireme is as follows:
:All waiters are beneficent '''''because they cater to the needs of their customers.'''''
:Darryl is a waiter '''''since Darryl serves tables at Chez Casimir'''''
:Therefore, Darryl is beneficent.
